summary: Onnellinen aviomies by Karl August Görner is a three-act comedic play written in the mid-19th century. It centers on a farcical impersonation scheme in an artist’s household when a carefree friend tries to “borrow” a wife to deceive his rich uncle. The key figures are the placid painter Reino Aarnio, his conscientious wife Elli, Elli’s sharp sister Laura, the prodigal Heikki Tuulispää, and Heikki’s uncle Petäjä, whose visit sparks a cascade of deceptions about marriage, money, and respectability. The opening of the play shows Aarnio painting while Elli good‑naturedly lectures him on husbands’ habits, then Laura breezes in with flirtatious letters before the exuberant Heikki barrels onto the scene with a trunk and a crisis: he has long pretended to be married to tap his uncle’s generosity, and the uncle is arriving that very day. Heikki begs to borrow Aarnio’s household; Elli refuses to play the wife but lends the home and nudges Laura to impersonate Heikki’s spouse for three days. When Uncle Petäjä arrives, Laura first performs the model homemaker—adjusting his collar, planning menus, even lighting his pipe—while Heikki scrambles to cover contradictions in his past fabrications (her name, her father, a melodramatic elopement). Elli fumes about smoking and disorder, Heikki ostentatiously praises her to sway the uncle, and Laura vows to switch from sweetness to shrewishness as needed to make the ruse work—setting the stage for the coming complications.
